speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, did you hear a specific "pop" or "snap" sound in your right groin or hip at the moment of the rear-end collision?

REQUEST TEST: Right Hip X-Ray (AP and Frog-leg lateral views)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray findings indicate no fractures in the pelvic ring or femoral neck; however, alignment suggests a posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the X-ray results. Can you describe your current leg position, and is the right thigh shorter or rotated inward compared to the left?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Dislocation of the Right Hip.

Please confirm that the right foot is pointing inward (adducted and internally rotated) and that the leg appears shortened, as this is the classic presentation for this injury.
